A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same evolving work on automatically generated vocabularies for 3D segmentation and retain TPSS. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v2 has no appendix; v3 includes readable supplementary Sections S1-S7.

before.justification: v2 reports original AutoVoc3D segmentation and TPSS results on nuScenes in Tables 1-2, alongside qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v3 reports original 3D-AVS results on nuScenes, ScanNet and ScanNet200, including component ablations, challenging-condition analyses and vocabulary-mapper comparisons in the supplement.

M1.justification: v2 combines AutoSeg's BLIP-based image queries with distilled OpenScene segmentation. v3 replaces the image captioner with xGen-MM and adds a trainable point captioner with Sparse Masked Attention Pooling, CLIP feature distillation and geometric sector/pillar masks. It supports image-independent inference and optional fusion of image and point similarities, substantially changing the procedure.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates only outdoor nuScenes data. v3 retains nuScenes and adds indoor ScanNet evaluation with 20-class and ScanNet200 200-class annotations. The paper explicitly states that these indoor evaluations share input point clouds and predictions; ScanNet200 adds finer label requirements rather than an independent collection of scenes.

E2.justification: The nuScenes comparison removes LidarMultiNet, MinkowskiNet and MSeg Voting, retains OpenScene, and adds CLIP2Scene, HICL, AdaCo and CNS. v3's indoor comparisons also include ConceptFusion, OpenMask3D and Diff2Scene (Table 2). LidarCLIP is newly evaluated against the point captioner in Table S2.

E3.justification: v2 evaluates mapped segmentation using LAVE with Llama-2-7B and reports mIoU and mAcc. v3 uses GPT-4o mapping for its main results and omits mAcc. New evaluation designs compare modalities and geometric partitions, stratify nuScenes by lighting/weather, and check automated mapping against manual mapping on ten ScanNet scenes containing 125 generated categories.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's illustrative outdoor comparisons, v3 adds controlled studies of captioner choice, compound nouns, positional encoding, sector count and pillar size (Tables S1-S3). It also analyzes captioner fusion, night/rain performance, and sensitivity to automated versus manual vocabulary mapping (Figure 5 and Sections S4-S5), substantially expanding diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. v3's expanded tables and condition-wise bar chart retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The reported nuScenes result changes from AutoVoc3D's 30.6 mIoU in v2 Table 1 to 3D-AVS's 36.2 in v3 Table 2. Because the method and mapping protocol change, this is not an established same-setting improvement. v3 additionally reports 40.5 mIoU on ScanNet and 14.6 on ScanNet200, plus extensive modality, ablation, mapper and qualitative results.

T1.justification: v3 adds local mathematical definitions for multimodal label assignment, angular sector masks and masked feature transformation (Equations 5-7). TPSS retains the same mean of per-point maximum similarities, despite renotation and reordered exposition. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand from an image-driven AutoSeg/OpenScene adaptation to a framework featuring a new point captioner, SMAP, image-independent recognition and robustness under challenging lighting. v2's conclusion claims no additional training; v3 instead includes a trained component. Automatic vocabulary generation and TPSS remain central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking geometric captioning to low-light resilience and attributes weaker ScanNet performance to coarse vocabulary mapping. It also acknowledges limited indoor category recognition by the point captioner and memory constraints for finer pillars (Sections 5.2-5.3 and S3-S4). These substantially extend v2's discussion of precise naming and information lost through mapping.

D1.justification: v3 Section S2 specifies the captioning prompt, temperature 0.05, five beams, pretrained encoder weights, MSE loss, learning rate, decay schedule, 20/10 training epochs and geometric partition sizes. Section 5.1 newly documents 0.5-second nuScenes point aggregation. v2 supplies much less implementation information; its silence on aggregation does not establish that preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around image and point-cloud captioning, including xGen-MM, ClipCap and LidarCLIP, and adds CaSED and concurrent PoVo. Section 2 distinguishes its vocabulary-generation approach from PoVo's cluster-first instance segmentation and positions SMAP against LidarCLIP's single global caption, extending v2's narrower AutoSeg/OpenScene framing.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming AutoVoc3D to 3D-AVS, v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, contributions and method narrative, restructures related work, and divides experiments into setup, vocabulary comparison, segmentation comparison and ablations. TPSS and vocabulary mapping exchange order within Evaluation, and the new supplement organizes implementation, analyses and nomenclature.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the outdoor visualizations and teaser, adding a vocabulary-size chart. It replaces the simple task schematic with a detailed pipeline and adds point-captioner and SMAP diagrams, a condition-wise chart and indoor/weather examples. Tables are reorganized around multiple datasets and modalities, with new supplementary ablation, class-wise and mapper displays.

improvement.justification: v2 provides limited pipeline validation and no direct check of its vocabulary mapper. v3 substantially strengthens validation through component ablations, modality/condition tests, indoor evaluation and comparison with manual mapping, while S2 improves implementation transparency. Some claims need qualification: Table S5 reports 44.38 mIoU for image-only ScanNet predictions versus 40.51 for fusion, and Table S4 gives fused man-made IoU as 53.5 rather than the prose's 55.4. These reporting weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in supporting evidence and reproducibility information.
